updates.bio: Started at the San Francisco Estuary Partnership (SFEP) in 2011 in a senior planning role and became its director in 2015, per SFEP's biography page. updates.name: Caitlyn Florentine
updates.bio: Research physical scientist at the U.S. Geological Survey Northern Rocky Mountain Science Center in Bozeman, Montana. Studies glaciers and snow by pairing field measurements with remote sensing and simple numerical models, emphasizing ice-flow physics and how glaciers respond to climate. Contributes to the USGS Glaciers and Climate Project; Ph.D. in geosciences, University of Montana (2018).
updates.research_interests: quantitative glaciology; glacier flow physics; glacier-climate relationships; avalanche science; alpine and Arctic geomorphology and hydrology

His listed publications address wetland and peatland carbon, mangrove carbon stocks and fluxes, hydrology of low-gradient coastal-plain forested watersheds, and longleaf pine restoration and water yield on the Santee Experimental Forest.

updates.name: Carl Gouldman
updates.bio: Directed the U.S. IOOS (Integrated Ocean Observing System) Program Office from February 2017 after serving as its deputy from 2014. Joined NOAA in 2000 at the Coastal Services Center and in 2004 became the first permanent IOOS employee. In April 2025 he announced his departure from NOAA after 25 years with IOOS.

updates.name: Carl J. Bernacchi
updates.bio: Professor of Crop Sciences and Plant Biology at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and director of phenotyping for the RIPE photosynthesis project. Investigates how rising CO2, ozone, drought and other stresses alter Midwest crop physiology, using eddy covariance to measure ecosystem carbon exchange; runs two flux towers at Bondville, Illinois, and works on SoyFACE experiments.
updates.research_interests: crop physiology under climate change; elevated CO2 and ozone effects on soybean (SoyFACE); canopy-atmosphere energy fluxes; eddy covariance net ecosystem carbon exchange; carbon sequestration in Midwest agriculture; crop responses to drought and insect stress; photosynthesis

updates.name: Catherine M. Pringle
updates.bio: Distinguished Research Professor and Professor Emerita at the University of Georgia Odum School of Ecology. Her stream ecology research examines how disturbances such as dams, disease, land-use and climate change reshape flowing-water ecosystems, through long-term site-based studies in temperate and tropical streams and electric-exclosure experiments testing the role of fish, crayfish and shrimp.
updates.research_interests: disturbance effects on stream ecosystems (dams, disease, land use, climate); hydrologic connectivity; macroconsumer top-down effects via electric exclosures; nutrient cycling; tropical streams (Puerto Rico, Costa Rica); aquatic conservation and habitat restoration

updates.name: Catherine R. Edwards
updates.bio: Associate Professor at the University of Georgia Skidaway Institute of Oceanography, working in coastal physical oceanography and marine robotics. Combines observations and models to study continental-shelf circulation, including sea- and land-breeze forcing near the critical latitude, diurnal heating and mixing, and their effects on larval transport and nutrient budgets. Ph.D., UNC Chapel Hill (2008).
updates.research_interests: coastal and continental-shelf physical oceanography; marine robotics; sea/land-breeze forcing and diurnal-inertial resonance near the critical latitude; air-sea interaction and mixing; larval transport and nutrient budgets
